en: The wooden ramp used to load rice sacks onto trucks in Nueva Ecija acts as an inclined plane to reduce lifting force.
The rough rubber soles of Filipino tsinelas increase friction to prevent slipping on wet palengke floors.
Earth's gravity pulls falling Guimaras carabao mangoes straight down to the ground once they detach from the tree.
The black sand beaches of Cagayan contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that is strongly attracted to magnets.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts underground volcanic heat into electricity to power homes in Luzon.
Fireflies along Bohol's Loboc River produce visible light through a chemical reaction in their abdomens called bioluminescence.
Striking the brass kulintang gongs in Mindanao causes the metal to vibrate and produce musical sound waves.
Cooking sinigang in a metal kawa pot transfers thermal energy from the hot stove to the soup through conduction.
A flying saranggola kite in Pampanga possesses kinetic energy because of its continuous motion through the wind.
Plucking the strings of a kudyapi lute in Mindanao transforms mechanical energy from the musician's fingers into sound energy.
The gravitational pull of the moon causes the ocean water in Manila Bay to rise and fall during tides.
The hot springs in Los Banos, Laguna, transfer geothermal heat to the water through conduction from deep underground rocks.
